claim: Circular RNAs (circRNAs) act through multiple mechanisms via their sequence features to fine-tune gene expression networks.
source: Circular RNAs (circRNAs) act through multiple mechanisms via their sequence features to fine-tune gene expression networks.
evidence: This is a general statement about circRNA function that is presented as established knowledge in the abstract.

claim: Identifying internal sequences of circRNAs remains a challenge due to overlapping sequences with linear cognates.
source: Due to overlapping sequences with linear cognates, identifying internal sequences of circRNAs remains a challenge, which hinders a comprehensive understanding of circRNA functions and mechanisms.
evidence: This statement describes a known limitation in the field based on the nature of circRNA sequences.

claim: circFL-seq is a full-length circRNA sequencing method based on rolling circular reverse transcription and nanopore sequencing.
source: Here, based on rolling circular reverse transcription and nanopore sequencing, we developed circFL-seq, a full-length circRNA sequencing method, to profile circRNA at the isoform level.
evidence: This describes the method developed in this study.

claim: circFL-seq reconstructed 77,606 high-quality circRNAs from seven human cell lines and two human tissues.
source: With a customized computational pipeline to directly identify full-length sequences from rolling circular reads, we reconstructed 77,606 high-quality circRNAs from seven human cell lines and two human tissues.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the study's data analysis.

claim: circFL-seq showed more than tenfold enrichment of circRNA reads compared to short-read RNA sequencing.
source: circFL-seq benefits from rolling circles and long-read sequencing, and the results showed more than tenfold enrichment of circRNA reads and advantages for both detection and quantification at the isoform level compared to those for short-read RNA sequencing.
evidence: This is a comparative quantitative finding from the study.

claim: circFL-seq has advantages for both detection and quantification at the isoform level compared to short-read RNA sequencing.
source: circFL-seq benefits from rolling circles and long-read sequencing, and the results showed more than tenfold enrichment of circRNA reads and advantages for both detection and quantification at the isoform level compared to those for short-read RNA sequencing.
evidence: This is a comparative assessment based on the study's results.

claim: The concordance of RT-qPCR and circFL-seq results for identification of differential alternative splicing suggests wide application prospects for functional studies of internal variants in circRNAs.
source: The concordance of the RT-qPCR and circFL-seq results for the identification of differential alternative splicing suggested wide application prospects for functional studies of internal variants in circRNAs.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the validation experiments comparing two methods.

claim: circFL-seq can detect fusion circRNAs at the omics scale.
source: Moreover, the detection of fusion circRNAs at the omics scale may further expand the application of circFL-seq.
evidence: This describes a capability demonstrated in the study.

claim: circRNAs are formed via back-splicing or lariat precursors.
source: Circular RNAs (circRNAs), a class of covalently closed RNA molecules formed via back-splicing (BS) or lariat precursors, are involved in various biological processes and pathogenesis by fine-tuning the eukaryotic gene regulatory network (Kristensen et al., 2019; Chen, 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: circRNAs are involved in various biological processes and pathogenesis by fine-tuning the eukaryotic gene regulatory network.
source: Circular RNAs (circRNAs), a class of covalently closed RNA molecules formed via back-splicing (BS) or lariat precursors, are involved in various biological processes and pathogenesis by fine-tuning the eukaryotic gene regulatory network (Kristensen et al., 2019; Chen, 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: circRNAs may complementarily bind to miRNAs as sponges.
source: For example, circRNAs may complementarily bind to miRNAs as sponges (Hansen et al., 2013; Memczak et al., 2013)
evidence: This mechanism is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: circRNAs may interact with proteins as scaffolds or structural components based on sequence motifs.
source: circRNAs may interact with proteins as scaffolds (Du et al., 2017) or structural components (Li et al., 2015) based on sequence motifs
evidence: This mechanism is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Several circRNAs are able to translate into peptides through internal ribosome entry sites.
source: and several circRNAs are also able to translate into peptides (Zhang et al., 2018; Gao et al., 2021 ) through internal ribosome entry sites.
evidence: This capability is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Full-length sequences of circRNAs are the foundation for ascertaining their biological functions in transcriptional plasticity and complexity.
source: Thus, full-length sequences of circRNAs have become the foundation for ascertaining their biological functions in transcriptional plasticity and complexity.
evidence: This is a logical inference based on the relationship between sequence and function.

claim: Short-read RNA sequencing discriminates circRNAs with low expression (as low as 1% polyadenylated RNA) from their linear cognates by detecting back-splicing junctions.
source: By detecting the back-splicing junctions (BSJs) of circRNAs with deep sequencing, short-read RNA sequencing discriminates circRNAs with low expression (as low as 1% polyadenylated RNA; Salzman et al., 2013) from their linear cognates.
evidence: This describes a capability of short-read sequencing supported by a citation.

claim: The full-length sequences of short circRNAs (<500 nt) can be inferred from a patchwork of BSJs and short fragments via bioinformatic approaches.
source: The full-length sequences of short circRNAs (<500 nt) can be inferred from a patchwork of BSJs and short fragments via bioinformatic approaches (Zheng et al., 2019; Wu et al., 2019b).
evidence: This describes a computational approach supported by citations.

claim: A full understanding of circRNA isoforms is impossible by using short reads.
source: However, a full understanding of circRNA isoforms is impossible by using short reads.
evidence: This is a limitation inferred from the nature of short-read sequencing technology.

claim: Single-molecule long-read sequencing has shown methodological advances in identifying circRNAs at the isoform level.
source: Single-molecule long-read sequencing has shown methodological advances in identifying circRNAs at the isoform level.
evidence: This is a general statement about technological advances in the field.

claim: Pacific Biosciences (PacBio) sequencing has been applied to PCR products for target full-length circRNA sequences in a low-throughput and high-cost way.
source: Pacific Biosciences (PacBio) sequencing has been applied to PCR products for target full-length circRNA sequences in a low-throughput and high-cost way (You et al., 2015).
evidence: This describes a previous method supported by a citation.

claim: Several Oxford Nanopore Technology (ONT)-based methods have been employed in genome-wide full-length circRNA reconstruction.
source: Very recently, several Oxford Nanopore Technology (ONT)-based methods have also been employed in genome-wide full-length circRNA reconstruction (Rahimi et al., 2019; Xin et al., 2021a; Zhang et al., 2021a).
evidence: This describes recent methods supported by citations.

claim: Eight known circRNAs were selected for PCR validation in the HEK293T library.
source: To benchmark full-length circRNA sequences of the circFL-seq library, eight known circRNAs were selected for PCR validation in the HEK293T library.
evidence: This describes an experimental validation step performed in the study.

claim: Rolling circles of target circRNA and full-length sequences obtained with Sanger sequencing indicated that the circRNAs were successfully amplified.
source: Rolling circles of target circRNA (Figure 1B; Figure 1—source data 1) and the full-length sequences obtained with Sanger sequencing (Figure 1—figure supplement 1) indicated that the circRNAs were successfully amplified.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: circFL-seq applied to eight libraries produced 30 M clean reads sequenced by using one PromethION Flow Cell.
source: To assess the performance of circFL-seq, we applied circFL-seq to eight libraries of six human cell lines (two replicates from HeLa cells, two replicates from SKOV3 cells, one from MCF7 cells, one from VCaP cells, one from SH-SY5Y cells, and one from HEK293T cells) and produced 30 M clean reads sequenced by using one PromethION Flow Cell (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the sequencing experiment.

claim: circFL-seq detected 197,252 isoforms of 162,409 circRNA BSJs from 1.3 M reads that contained full-length circRNA sequences.
source: We detected 197,252 isoforms of 162,409 circRNA BSJs from 1.3 M reads that contained full-length circRNA sequences (Figure 2A; Figure 2—figure supplement 1B; Figure 2—figure supplement 2A; Supplementary file 1)
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the data analysis.

claim: 2% of circRNA isoforms were additionally detected by cRG mode, which refined low-quality reads with consensus sequences.
source: 2% of which were additionally detected by cRG mode, which refined low-quality reads with CS (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B-D).
evidence: This is a quantitative result showing the contribution of the cRG mode.

claim: Quantification of replicate samples at both the BSJ and isoform levels was highly consistent (Pearson's r>0.93).
source: Quantification of replicate samples at both the BSJ and isoform levels was highly consistent (Pearson's r>0.93; Figure 2A and B; Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a statistical measure of reproducibility from the data.

claim: The exonic type accounted for 73.2% of the identified circRNA species for high-quality circRNA isoforms (read counts≥5).
source: For high-quality circRNA isoforms (read counts≥5), the exonic type accounted for 73.2% of the identified circRNA species, while only 0.1% were from read-through (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the classification of circRNAs.

claim: Most exonic types (99.8%) could be verified in at least one database.
source: Most exonic types (99.8%) could be verified in at least one database (Glažar et al., 2014; Chen et al., 2016; Dong et al., 2018; Liu et al., 2019; Vo et al., 2019; Huang et al., 2021; Figure 2C)
evidence: This is a validation result comparing detected circRNAs to existing databases.

claim: The median length of circRNA types varied from 402 nt of the intergenic type to 618 nt of read-throughs.
source: The median length of each type varied from 402 nt of the intergenic type to 618 nt of read-throughs (Figure 2D)
evidence: This is a quantitative result describing circRNA length distributions.

claim: A notable proportion of circRNAs>500 nt cannot be reconstructed by RNA-seq.
source: The median length of each type varied from 402 nt of the intergenic type to 618 nt of read-throughs (Figure 2D), indicating that a notable proportion of circRNAs>500 nt cannot be reconstructed by RNA-seq.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the length distribution data and known limitations of RNA-seq.

claim: Read-through circRNAs contained more exons than other types.
source: Read-through circRNAs contained more exons (Figure 2E)
evidence: This is a comparative result from the structural analysis.

claim: The exon length of single-exon circRNA was significantly longer than that of multiple-exon circRNA (p<2.2×10–16).
source: while the exon length of single-exon circRNA was significantly longer than that of multiple-exon circRNA (p<2.2×10–16; Figure 2F).
evidence: This is a statistical comparison of exon lengths.

claim: From 65,656 isoforms of 35,251 high-quality circRNA BSJs (read counts≥5), 23,267 internal AS events were identified.
source: From 65,656 isoforms of 35,251 high-quality circRNA BSJs (read counts≥5), we identified 23,267 internal AS events (Supplementary file 2)
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the alternative splicing analysis.

claim: Internal AS events included 44.3% exon skipping (ES), 28.1% alternative 3′ splicing site (A3SS), 24.1% alternative 5′ splicing site (A5SS), and 3.5% intron retention (IR) events.
source: including 44.3% exon skipping (ES), 28.1% alternative 3′ splicing site (A3SS), 24.1% alternative 5′ splicing site (A5SS), and 3.5% intron retention (IR) events (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is a quantitative breakdown of AS event types.

claim: IR events increased circRNA length by 289 nt on average (from 363 to 652 nt).
source: Specifically, IR events increased circRNA length by 289 nt on average (from 363 to 652 nt), which may influence their cellular localization (Huang et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the analysis of IR events.

claim: IR events may influence circRNA cellular localization.
source: Specifically, IR events increased circRNA length by 289 nt on average (from 363 to 652 nt), which may influence their cellular localization (Huang et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a speculation supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: circFL-seq accurately detected the full length of two isoforms (1485 and 1301 nt) generated by the IR event of CDR1as.
source: circFL-seq accurately detected the full length of two isoforms (1485 and 1301 nt) generated by the IR event of CDR1as (Hansen et al., 2011; Figure 2H).
evidence: This is a specific example of circRNA detection validated by the data.

claim: 13 AS events (5 of ES, 3 of A3SS, 1 of A5SS, and 4 of IR) of 23 isoforms from 11 high-quality circRNAs in the HeLa cell line were experimentally verified.
source: We further experimentally verified 13 AS events (5 of ES, 3 of A3SS, 1 of A5SS, and 4 of IR) of 23 isoforms from 11 high-quality circRNAs in the HeLa cell line.
evidence: This describes experimental validation performed in the study.

claim: All but an A3SS event were validated by Sanger sequencing.
source: With divergent primers to amplify both BSJs and alternative spliced forward splicing junctions (FSJs), all but an A3SS event were validated by Sanger sequencing (Figure 2I–K; Figure 2—figure supplements 6–8).
evidence: This is a result from the experimental validation.

claim: Eight RNA-seq libraries (150 bp×2) with the same circRNA enrichment method for the same six cell lines were generated and sequenced by the Illumina HiSeq X Ten platform.
source: Thus, for comparison, eight RNA-seq libraries (150 bp×2) with the same circRNA enrichment method for the same six cell lines (Pearson's r>0.90 for replicates, Figure 3—figure supplement 1) were generated and sequenced by the Illumina HiSeq X Ten platform.
evidence: This describes the experimental design for comparison.

claim: A total of 95,371 circRNA BSJs were detected by CIRI2 from RNA-seq data.
source: A total of 95,371 circRNA BSJs were detected by CIRI2 (Gao et al., 2018; Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the RNA-seq analysis.

claim: BSJ reads accounted for 0.15–0.32% of all RNA-seq reads, an amount 10 times lower than that of full-length circRNA reads with circFL-seq (2.2–8.5%).
source: BSJ reads accounted for 0.15–0.32% of all RNA-seq reads, an amount 10 times lower than that of full-length circRNA reads with circFL-seq (2.2–8.5%).
evidence: This is a comparative quantitative result between the two methods.

claim: The proportion of overlapping BSJs identified by RNA-seq seemed to be larger than that identified by circFL-seq (76.7% vs. 40.3%) when compared to known BSJs annotated in the database.
source: Compared to known BSJs that have been annotated in the database, the proportion of overlapping BSJs identified by RNA-seq seemed to be larger than that identified by circFL-seq (76.7% vs. 40.3%) (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a comparative result from the database validation.

claim: When focusing on high-quality BSJs (read counts≥5), the proportion obtained with circFL-seq (78.9%) was similar to that obtained with RNA-seq.
source: However, when focusing on high-quality BSJs (read counts≥5), the proportion obtained with circFL-seq (78.9%) was similar to that obtained with RNA-seq, indicating that more reads are required to confidently identify circRNAs by ONT (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a comparative result showing the effect of read depth.

claim: More reads are required to confidently identify circRNAs by ONT.
source: However, when focusing on high-quality BSJs (read counts≥5), the proportion obtained with circFL-seq (78.9%) was similar to that obtained with RNA-seq, indicating that more reads are required to confidently identify circRNAs by ONT (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the comparison of detection rates at different read depths.

claim: The full-length construction by RNA-seq was highly dependent on circRNA length.
source: As expected, the full-length construction by RNA-seq was highly dependent on circRNA length (Figure 3—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is a result from the comparison showing a limitation of RNA-seq.

claim: Approximately 96.3% of full-length circRNAs reconstructed by RNA-seq were less than 500 nt in length.
source: Approximately 96.3% of full-length circRNAs reconstructed by RNA-seq were less than 500 nt in length, while 44.4% of circRNA isoforms detected by circFL-seq were more than 500 nt in length.
evidence: This is a quantitative comparison of the length distributions.

claim: 44.4% of circRNA isoforms detected by circFL-seq were more than 500 nt in length.
source: Approximately 96.3% of full-length circRNAs reconstructed by RNA-seq were less than 500 nt in length, while 44.4% of circRNA isoforms detected by circFL-seq were more than 500 nt in length.
evidence: This is a quantitative result showing the advantage of circFL-seq for longer circRNAs.

claim: circFL-seq produced more full-length circRNA reads per 10^9 raw bases than isoCirc (11,791 vs. 5820).
source: circFL-seq produced more full-length circRNA reads per 109 raw bases than isoCirc (11,791 vs. 5820) (Figure 3—figure supplement 5A-C)
evidence: This is a quantitative comparison of efficiency between methods.

claim: circFL-seq identified fewer circRNA isoforms than isoCirc in the HEK293 cell line comparison.
source: but identified fewer circRNA isoforms (Figure 3—figure supplement 5D).
evidence: This is a quantitative comparison of detection between methods.

claim: 75.3% of circFL-seq-detected BSJs were annotated in the database, while the percentage of isoCirc was 43.8%.
source: However, 75.3% of circFL-seq-detected BSJs were annotated in the database, while the percentage of isoCirc was 43.8% (Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This is a comparative validation result using database annotations.

claim: All the top 100 expressed BSJs identified by circFL-seq and RNA-seq were annotated in databases.
source: All the top 100 expressed BSJs identified by circFL-seq and RNA-seq (collected from isoCirc study) were annotated in databases.
evidence: This is a validation result for highly expressed circRNAs.

claim: 22 of the top 100 BSJs identified by isoCirc were not supported in the databases or the RNA-seq and circFL-seq results.
source: In contrast, 22 of the top 100 BSJs identified by isoCirc were not supported in the databases or the RNA-seq and circFL-seq results (Figure 3—figure supplement 5M).
evidence: This is a comparative validation result suggesting potential false positives in isoCirc.

claim: At the isoform level in the HEK293 cell line, 87.0% of the common BSJs (10,702/12,307) between circFL-seq and isoCirc identified at least one identical isoform.
source: At the isoform level in the HEK293 cell line, 87.0% of the common BSJs (10,702/12,307) between circFL-seq and isoCirc identified at least one identical isoform.
evidence: This is a quantitative comparison of isoform concordance.

claim: circFL-seq identified more than two times ES, A3SS, and A5SS but similar numbers of IR events to isoCirc.
source: In addition, circFL-seq identified more than two times ES, A3SS, and A5SS but similar numbers of IR events to isoCirc (Supplementary file 4)
evidence: This is a comparative result for AS event detection.

claim: isoCirc and circFL-seq detected 79,312 and 34,046 known BSJs, respectively, in two normal human tissues (brain and testis).
source: isoCirc and circFL-seq detected 79,312 and 34,046 known BSJs, respectively.
evidence: This is a quantitative comparison in tissue samples.

claim: Known BSJs detected by isoCirc were more likely (38,846 vs. 2511) to be expressed at low levels (read counts=1).
source: Known BSJs detected by isoCirc were more likely (38,846 vs. 2511) to be expressed at low levels (read counts=1), indicating that more libraries were more sensitive for detecting circRNAs, overcoming bias and artifacts related to sampling, RNase R treatment, cDNA synthesis, and amplification.
evidence: This is a comparative result with an inference about the effect of multiple libraries.

claim: The computational pipeline of circFL-seq was more sensitive with similar precision for BSJ detection compared to CIRI-long.
source: Thus, the computational pipeline of circFL-seq was more sensitive with similar precision for BSJ detection.
evidence: This is a comparative assessment of the computational methods.

claim: For AS events, circFL-seq identified more than 4.5 times the ES events, 12.4 times the A3SS events, 8.5 times the A5SS events, and 1.5 times the IR events compared to CIRI-long.
source: For AS events, circFL-seq identified more than 4.5 times the ES events, 12.4 times the A3SS events, 8.5 times the A5SS events, and 1.5 times the IR events, suggesting a better sensitivity of circFL-seq in AS event detection, although ground-truth circRNA isoforms were required for performance evaluation (Supplementary file 5).
evidence: This is a comparative result for AS event detection.

claim: For BSJs identified by circFL-seq and RNA-seq, the amounts between the two methods were significantly correlated (Pearson's r=0.41–0.68).
source: For BSJs identified by circFL-seq and RNA-seq, the amounts between the two methods were significantly correlated (Pearson's r=0.41–0.68, Figure 3A; Figure 3—figure supplement 6).
evidence: This is a statistical measure of correlation for quantification.

claim: For highly expressed BSJs, the fold changes in HeLa to SKOV3 cells were highly concordant with the RNA-seq results (Pearson's r=0.78).
source: For the highly expressed BSJs (read counts≥10 in at least two samples and detected by both methods), the fold changes in HeLa to SKOV3 cells were highly concordant with the RNA-seq results (Pearson's r=0.78, Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a statistical measure of concordance for differential expression.

claim: circFL-seq detected 89 DECs, 58 of which were also identified by RNA-seq.
source: By using DESeq2 (Love et al., 2014), circFL-seq detected 89 DECs, 58 of which were also identified by RNA-seq.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from differential expression analysis.

claim: The consistent circFL-seq and RT-qPCR results for both total RNA and RNase R-treated samples supported the capabilities of BSJ quantification.
source: The consistent circFL-seq and RT-qPCR results for both total RNA (Figure 3—figure supplement 7A-C) and RNase R-treated (Figure 3C and D) samples further supported the capabilities of BSJ quantification.
evidence: This is a validation result comparing two quantification methods.

claim: From 87 BSJs that had at least two isoforms detected by both HeLa and SKOV3 cell lines, 193 isoforms were used to quantify the internal variants by the ratio of transcripts.
source: From 87 BSJs that had at least two isoforms detected by both HeLa and SKOV3 cell lines, 193 isoforms were used to quantify the internal variants by the ratio of transcripts (target isoforms to total isoforms from the same BSJ).
evidence: This describes the analysis approach for isoform quantification.

claim: 90 transcripts had more than 0.1 ratio differences between HeLa and SKOV3 cell lines.
source: A total of 90 transcripts had more than 0.1 ratio differences between HeLa and SKOV3 cell lines.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the differential isoform analysis.

claim: circ-PLOD2 showed a higher ratio of transcripts without ES in the HeLa cell line (0.83 to 0.45).
source: For example, circ-PLOD2 showed a higher ratio of transcripts without ES in the HeLa cell line (0.83 to 0.45) (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is a specific example of differential isoform expression.

claim: Both the transcript ratios and ratio differences were consistent with the RT-qPCR results for 18 isoforms of 9 circRNA BSJs.
source: Both the transcript ratios and ratio differences were consistent with the RT-qPCR results (Figure 3F and G; Figure 3—figure supplement 7D-F), supporting the advantage of circFL-seq for quantification at the isoform level.
evidence: This is a validation result for isoform quantification.

claim: circFL-seq was able to detect f-circRNA with rolling circular reads separately mapped to two loci in different chromosomes or a >1 Mbp distance in the same chromosome.
source: circFL-seq was able to detect f-circRNA with rolling circular reads separately mapped to two loci in different chromosomes or a >1 Mbp distance in the same chromosome (Figure 4A).
evidence: This describes the capability of the method for detecting fusion circRNAs.

claim: Six high-quality f-circRNA isoforms (read count≥5) affiliated with two fusion genes were identified in the MCF7 cell line.
source: With circFL-seq data, we identified six high-quality f-circRNA isoforms (read count≥5) affiliated with two fusion genes in the MCF7 cell line.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the fusion circRNA analysis.

claim: The rolling circles of full-length sequences of two major isoforms from GBF1/MACROD2 fusion were validated by Sanger sequencing.
source: As expected, more than one product was observed (Figure 4C), and the rolling circles of full-length sequences were validated by Sanger sequencing (Figure 4D, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an experimental validation result.

claim: The fusion junction of E2–E4 was validated with linear RNA as a template, suggesting the existence of linear RNA production from the fusion gene.
source: Intriguingly, we validated the fusion junction of E2–E4 with linear RNA as a template (Figure 4C), suggesting the existence of linear RNA production from the fusion gene.
evidence: This is an experimental result with an inference about the fusion gene.

claim: The decreased expression of junctions E2–E4 after RNase R treatment supported the linear production, which further suggested that the fusion direction is GBF1 to MACROD2.
source: The decreased expression of junctions E2–E4 after RNase R treatment also supported the linear production, which further suggested that the fusion direction is GBF1 to MACROD2 (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the RNase R treatment experiment.

claim: The f-circRNA fused by two antisense genes (PRICKLE2-AS1 and PTPRT-AS1) was experimentally validated.
source: In addition, the f-circRNA fused by two antisense genes (PRICKLE2-AS1 and PTPRT-AS1) was experimentally validated (Figure 4F; Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is an experimental validation result.

claim: All the major fusion junctions of GBF1/MACROD2 and E3-E1 of PRICKLE2-AS1/PTPRT-AS1 were validated by RNA-seq of the MCF7 cell line.
source: All the major fusion junctions of GBF1/MACROD2 and E3-E1 of PRICKLE2-AS1/PTPRT-AS1 were validated by RNA-seq of the MCF7 cell line (Figure 4G).
evidence: This is a validation result using RNA-seq data.

claim: Long-read sequencing with circFL-seq has shown advances in comprehensively identifying full-length circRNAs of all sizes (64–2334 nt in our data and more than 40% identified isoforms >500 nt) compared to short-read sequencing.
source: Compared to short-read sequencing, which is limited to reconstructing short circRNAs (<500 nt), long-read sequencing with circFL-seq has shown advances in comprehensively identifying full-length circRNAs of all sizes (64–2334 nt in our data and more than 40% identified isoforms >500 nt).
evidence: This is a comparative assessment of the method's capabilities.

claim: circFL-seq and CIRI-long employ the RCRT strategy, while isoCirc employs the RCA strategy.
source: circFL-seq and CIRI-long employ the RCRT strategy, while isoCirc employs the RCA strategy.
evidence: This is a comparison of methodological approaches.

claim: Benefiting from RCA with a circular cDNA template from ligation of the RT product, isoCirc produces longer reads (up to 50 kb) containing more rolling circles than RCRT-based methods (ca. 1 kb).
source: Benefiting from RCA with a circular cDNA template from ligation of the RT product, isoCirc produces longer reads (up to 50 kb) containing more rolling circles than RCRT-based methods (ca. 1 kb) and thus has an advantage in error correction during CS identification.
evidence: This is a comparative assessment of the methods based on their technical features.

claim: The cost of each full-length read is much higher in isoCirc than in circFL-seq and CIRI-long.
source: As a trade-off, the cost of each full-length read is much higher in isoCirc than in circFL-seq and CIRI-long.
evidence: This is an inference about the economic implications of the different methods.

claim: The unique ligation of cDNA in isoCirc may introduce false positives for circRNA detection by ligating cDNA from residual linear RNA or truncated cDNA of circRNA.
source: In addition, the unique ligation of cDNA in isoCirc may introduce false positives for circRNA detection by ligating cDNA from residual linear RNA or truncated cDNA of circRNA, which is hardly totally recognized and removed by computational analysis.
evidence: This is a speculation about a potential limitation of the isoCirc method.

claim: circFL-seq synthesizes second-strand cDNA with an anchor primer, while CIRI-long uses template switching.
source: However, circFL-seq synthesizes second-strand cDNA with an anchor primer, while CIRI-long uses template switching.
evidence: This is a comparison of technical details between methods.

claim: circFL-seq and CIRI-long are more resistant to the interference of residual linear RNA and generate shorter full-length reads of circRNA than isoCirc.
source: Thus, these two methods are more resistant to the interference of residual linear RNA and generate shorter full-length reads of circRNA than isoCirc.
evidence: This is an inference about the properties of the methods based on their technical features.

claim: RCRT-based methods are not as sensitive as isoCirc with the same number of full-length reads.
source: Thus, RCRT-based methods are not as sensitive as isoCirc with the same number of full-length reads.
evidence: This is an inference about the relative sensitivity of the methods.

claim: The RG mode of circFL-seq identified 56% more full-length circRNAs with fewer than two circles compared to methods that only use consensus sequences.
source: In contrast, the RG mode of circFL-seq identified 56% more full-length circRNAs with fewer than two circles in our data, which helps to improve the sensitivity of circRNA detection.
evidence: This is a quantitative result showing an advantage of the RG mode.

claim: circFL-seq leverages primer sequences to adjust the strand origin of circRNA, especially for BSJ with a non-canonical splicing motif.
source: In addition, circFL-seq leverages primer sequences to adjust the strand origin of circRNA, especially for BSJ with a non-canonical splicing motif.
evidence: This describes a technical feature of the circFL-seq method.

claim: circFL-seq was more sensitive than isoCirc and CIRI-long for AS detection.
source: In our comparisons, circFL-seq was more sensitive than isoCirc and CIRI-long for AS detection, although the performance required full evaluation by ground-truth circRNA isoforms.
evidence: This is a comparative assessment with a caveat about the need for further validation.

claim: f-circRNA has been found to play important roles in cancer pathogenesis.
source: Another novel application of full-length circRNA sequencing is to identify f-circRNA, which has been found to play important roles in cancer pathogenesis (Guarnerio et al., 2016)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: f-circRNA has become a promising biomarker for liquid biopsy.
source: and has become a promising biomarker for liquid biopsy (Tan et al., 2018a).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Current methods validated the proposed f-circRNA by designing divergent primers on known gene fusion junctions and thus were inefficient and possibly ignored f-circRNA from unknown gene fusions.
source: Current methods (Guarnerio et al., 2016; Tan et al., 2018a; Tan et al., 2018b; Wu et al., 2019a) validated the proposed f-circRNA by designing divergent primers on known gene fusion junctions and thus were inefficient and possibly ignored f-circRNA from unknown gene fusions.
evidence: This is a critique of existing methods supported by citations.

claim: circFL-seq showed its ability to high-throughput identify f-circRNA with cancer cell line data.
source: With cancer cell line data, circFL-seq showed its ability to high-throughput identify f-circRNA, which will promote our knowledge of f-circRNA.
